epic_n_patients_hepc.long_name: Number of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
epic_n_patients_hepc.short_description: Annual count of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
epic_n_patients_hepc.long_description: Count of distinct Epic Cosmos patients with at least one encounter in the calendar year who carry a viral hepatitis C diagnosis, by state of residence and age at encounter. The population base is all patients with any encounter and Country of Care = United States of America; no diagnosis filter is applied to the population, and the diagnosis restriction is applied as a row-level bucket so that the all-patients denominator (epic_n_patients) is reported alongside it. The diagnosis bucket was defined in SlicerDicer as ICD-10-CM B18.2 (chronic viral hepatitis C), B19.2 (unspecified viral hepatitis C), B17.1 (acute hepatitis C), and B17.2 (acute hepatitis E) as of the predecessor session; this has not been independently re-verified against the current session (2855468). B17.2 is not a hepatitis C code, so these counts likely contain a small number of acute hepatitis E patients; the bucket definition should be corrected and the session re-exported. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic Cosmos and imputed as 5 here, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag. The age value "Total" is the source's own overall-age total and includes patients whose age at encounter is unknown, so it exceeds the sum of the six age buckets by 1 to 2.5 percent; use the "Total" row for overall figures rather than summing the buckets. The most recent period may be a partial year, identifiable because its time value is not December 31 (currently 2026-08-18, covering January 1 to August 18 only). Counts for a partial period are NOT comparable to a full year. Use epic_pct_hepc for trend comparisons that include a partial period. As of the 2026-09-10 update (session 2855468), this series now covers 2018 onward with the age "Total" column throughout -- the earlier 2018-2019 NA gap from the predecessor session (2850163) is resolved. The underlying export also carries two additional measure columns per age bucket ("HepC diagnosis (%)" and a medication-within-6-months percentage) that are deliberately NOT captured here -- see ingest.R's CAVEAT comment for why.
epic_n_patients_hepc.statement: In {location}, {value} patients had a viral hepatitis C diagnosis in {time}.

epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the number of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the hepatitis C patient count was suppressed and imputed.
epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the cell (a count of 10 or fewer, reported as "10 or fewer") and the value was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. The flag is computed before imputation, so it records what the source withheld rather than what the ingest wrote. A flag of 1 always accompanies the imputed value 5, and no source-reported value carries a flag of 1.
epic_n_patients_hepc_suppressed_flag.statement: In {location}, the hepatitis C patient count for {time} was suppressed and imputed ({value}).

epic_n_patients.long_name: Number of patients with any encounter (denominator)
epic_n_patients.short_description: Annual count of all patients with any encounter, used as the hepatitis C denominator.
epic_n_patients.long_description: Count of distinct Epic Cosmos patients with at least one encounter in the calendar year, regardless of diagnosis, by state of residence and age at encounter. Taken from the per-state "Total" row of the diagnosis dimension in the SlicerDicer export, which includes all data under that state bucket. This is the denominator for epic_pct_hepc. Because it counts the full Epic Cosmos patient population rather than a census population, it reflects Epic's market share in each state and is not a general population count; state-to-state comparisons of the count itself are therefore not meaningful, though the derived percentage is comparable. The age value "Total" is the source's own overall-age total and includes patients of unknown age, so it exceeds the sum of the six buckets. Like the numerator, a count for a partial trailing period (time not ending December 31) covers only part of the year and is not comparable to a full year. Counts of 10 or fewer would be suppressed and imputed as 5; no denominator cell was suppressed in the current export.
epic_n_patients.statement: In {location}, {value} patients had at least one encounter in {time}.

epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the number of patients with any encounter
epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the all-patients denominator was suppressed and imputed.
epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the denominator cell (a count of 10 or fewer) and the value was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. Computed before imputation. Where this flag is 1, epic_pct_hepc is deliberately left missing rather than asserting the meaningless 5 / 5 = 100% that the imputed denominator would produce.
epic_n_patients_suppressed_flag.statement: In {location}, the all-patients denominator for {time} was suppressed and imputed ({value}).

epic_pct_hepc.long_name: Percent of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
epic_pct_hepc.short_description: Percent of patients with any encounter who have a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
epic_pct_hepc.long_description: Derived as epic_n_patients_hepc / epic_n_patients * 100 within each geography, year, and age group. Because both numerator and denominator come from the same Epic Cosmos patient population, this percentage is comparable across states and years in a way the raw counts are not. It measures diagnosed hepatitis C among patients who sought care, not population prevalence, and so is sensitive to testing and care-seeking patterns as well as to Epic's coverage in each state. Where the numerator was suppressed (10 or fewer), the imputed numerator of 5 carries through, which is equivalent to the 5 / denominator * 100 imputation rule; those cells are flagged by epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag. Where the denominator was suppressed, the value is left missing instead of computing 5 / 5 = 100%. Because numerator and denominator cover the same window, this measure is far more robust to a partial trailing period than the raw counts are, though it is still not strictly comparable to a full year, since a shorter observation window gives each patient fewer opportunities for a diagnosis to be recorded. Nationally (geography "00", age "Total") the rate has declined steadily: 0.45% (2018), 0.45% (2019), 0.42% (2020), 0.39% (2021), 0.38% (2022), 0.37% (2023), 0.36% (2024), 0.34% (2025), with the 2026-08-18 partial period at 0.32%. The underlying diagnosis bucket also includes ICD-10-CM B17.2 (acute hepatitis E) in error - see epic_n_patients_hepc.
epic_pct_hepc.statement: In {location}, {value}% of patients with an encounter in {time} had a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.

epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag.short_name: Suppressed flag: percent with hepatitis C
epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the percent of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis
epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the hepatitis C percentage rests on a suppressed and imputed value.
epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when either the numerator or the denominator of epic_pct_hepc was suppressed by Epic Cosmos; 0 otherwise. Computed before imputation. When only the numerator was suppressed, the percentage is reported using the imputed numerator of 5, matching the 5 / denominator * 100 rule. When the denominator was suppressed, epic_pct_hepc is left missing while this flag remains 1.
epic_pct_hepc_suppressed_flag.statement: In {location}, the hepatitis C percentage for {time} rests on a suppressed value ({value}).

epic_n_patients_hepc_medication.short_name: HCV medication patients meeting the measure
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication.long_name: Number of HCV-diagnosed patients who received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis (derived)
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication.short_description: Annual count of HCV-diagnosed patients who received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication.long_description: DERIVED, not directly reported by the source: computed as round(epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop * epic_pct_hepc_medication / 100). The source export gives this population's size (epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop) and its own rate, but not a numerator count, so this column reconstructs it from those two. The underlying population is ALL patients meeting the same viral hepatitis C diagnosis criteria as epic_n_patients_hepc (confirmed to match epic_n_patients_hepc cell-for-cell as of the 2026-09-10 update) -- NOT a smaller already-medicated subset; see epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop for the definition history. The diagnosis criteria previously included ICD-10-CM B17.2 (acute hepatitis E), which is not a hepatitis C code (see epic_n_patients_hepc's long_description); this has not been re-verified against the current session. This measure comes from a separate SlicerDicer session (2855386; predecessor 2850012) from epic_n_patients_hepc (2855468) with an independently set date range. Suppressed cells (source population of 10 or fewer, or a blank rate even when the population itself was shown) are imputed to 5, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag. The age value "Total" is the source's own overall-age total. The most recent period may be a partial year, identifiable because its time value is not December 31 (currently 2026-07-28, narrower than epic_n_patients_hepc's own 2026-08-18 partial period). Use epic_pct_hepc_medication for trend comparisons that include a partial period.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication.statement: In {location}, {value} HCV-diagnosed patients received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis in {time}.

epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppress.short_name: Suppressed flag: HCV medication patients meeting the measure
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppress.long_name: Suppression flag for the derived count of HCV medication patients meeting the measure
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppress.short_description: Indicates whether the underlying rate used to derive this count was suppressed and imputed.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppress.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the underlying cell (the population itself was 10 or fewer, or the population was shown but its rate was blank because the count meeting the measure was small enough to withhold on its own) and this derived value was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. The flag is computed before imputation, so it records what the source withheld rather than what the ingest wrote. A flag of 1 always accompanies the imputed value 5, and no source-reported value carries a flag of 1. This flag is identical to epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag, since both are derived from the same underlying rate.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppress.statement: In {location}, the HCV medication measure count for {time} was suppressed and imputed ({value}).

epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop.long_name: Number of patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis (denominator for epic_pct_hepc_medication)
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop.short_description: Annual count of HCV-diagnosed patients, used as the epic_pct_hepc_medication denominator.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop.long_description: Taken directly from the medication crosstab's "Number of Patients" column, by state of residence and age at encounter. As of the 2026-09-10 update (session 2855386), this population is applied as a session-level filter (viral hepatitis C diagnosis) rather than as a row-level bucket, and was CONFIRMED to match epic_n_patients_hepc cell-for-cell on every (geography, time, age) checked -- e.g. Texas / 2018 / 18-24 Years = 229 in both. This is a substantive change from the predecessor session (2850012), where this column instead reported a smaller, already-medicated subgroup ("has HCV medication" bucket); do not assume that older definition still applies. The diagnosis criteria previously included ICD-10-CM B17.2 (acute hepatitis E), which is not a hepatitis C code (see epic_n_patients_hepc's long_description); this has not been re-verified against the current session. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed and imputed as 5, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop_suppressed_flag. A count for a partial trailing period (time not ending December 31) covers only part of the year and is not comparable to a full year.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop.statement: In {location}, {value} patients had a viral hepatitis C diagnosis in {time} (medication crosstab).

epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop_supp.short_description: Indicates whether the population denominator was suppressed and imputed.
epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop_supp.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the denominator cell (a count of 10 or fewer) and the value was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. Computed before imputation. Where this flag is 1, epic_pct_hepc_medication is deliberately left missing rather than asserting the meaningless 5 / 5 = 100% that the imputed denominator would produce.

epic_pct_hepc_medication.long_name: Percent of HCV-diagnosed patients who received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis
epic_pct_hepc_medication.short_description: Rate of medication initiation within 6 months among all patients with a viral hepatitis C diagnosis.
epic_pct_hepc_medication.long_description: Taken directly from the medication crosstab's own rate column (imputed via the standard 5 / denominator rule when blank -- see below), NOT computed by this repo from two independently reported counts, since the source does not report the underlying numerator count directly (see epic_n_patients_hepc_medication, which instead derives a count FROM this percent). The denominator (epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop) is ALL patients meeting the same viral hepatitis C diagnosis criteria as epic_n_patients_hepc (confirmed to match it cell-for-cell as of the 2026-09-10 update) -- NOT a smaller already-medicated subset. The measure is: percent of these patients with 1 slice by any of a named set of HCV antiviral medications (ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir, elbasvir/grazoprevir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir) within 6 months of their diagnosis -- i.e. a treatment-initiation rate, as stated in the SlicerDicer session title. This is a SUBSTANTIVE DEFINITION CHANGE from the predecessor session (2850012): that session's rate (nationally 77-84 percent) was computed among an already-medicated subgroup and its exact clinical meaning was never confirmed; this session's rate is computed among all diagnosed patients and is explicitly a within-6-months treatment-initiation rate, so it is much lower in magnitude (nationally 14.5-17.5 percent, 2018-2025, trending upward) and NOT comparable to the old values -- do not chart them as a continuous series across this update. Where the underlying count was suppressed (10 or fewer, or a rate withheld even though the population was shown), the imputed rate is 5 / denominator * 100 and the cell is flagged by epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag. Where the denominator itself was suppressed, the value is left missing instead of computing 5 / 5 = 100%. The most recent period may be a partial year (currently 2026-07-28, narrower than epic_n_patients_hepc's own 2026-08-18 partial); use this percentage rather than the derived count for trend comparisons spanning the partial period, for the same reason described under epic_pct_hepc.
epic_pct_hepc_medication.statement: In {location}, {value}% of HCV-diagnosed patients in {time} received an HCV medication within 6 months of diagnosis.

epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag.short_name: Suppressed flag: HCV medication measure rate
epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag.long_name: Suppression flag for the hcv medication measure rate
epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag.short_description: Indicates whether the measure rate rests on a suppressed and imputed value.
epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 when the source's own rate was blank -- either because the population denominator itself was 10 or fewer, or because the count meeting the measure was small enough to withhold on its own even though the population was shown; 0 otherwise. Computed before imputation. When only the count was suppressed (population shown, rate blank), the rate is imputed as 5 / denominator * 100. When the denominator itself was suppressed, epic_pct_hepc_medication is left missing while this flag remains 1. This flag is identical to epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag, since both are derived from the same underlying rate.
epic_pct_hepc_medication_suppressed_flag.statement: In {location}, the hcv medication measure rate for {time} rests on a suppressed value ({value}).

epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis.long_name: Number of patients newly diagnosed with hepatitis C (no diagnosis in the prior year)
epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis.short_description: Annual count of NEW (incident) hepatitis C diagnoses -- patients diagnosed in the given year who were not already diagnosed the year before -- in the 5 geographies with any exported data.
epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis.long_description: Taken from a dedicated, consolidated SlicerDicer session (2857569) that reports 6 measures at once (this population size, plus 5 rates -- see epic_pct_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_hepc_abnormal_test_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_hepc_any_test_after_diagnosis, epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_diagnosis, epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_abnormal_new_diagnosis) cross-tabulated by state/year AND two additional row-bucket dimensions, (All) Lab Components in {"Hep C tests", Total} and All Medications in {"Hep C meds", Total}. Only the fully-unconditioned (Total x Total) row is kept here, per explicit user direction. The population is patients with a hepatitis C diagnosis in the given year who did NOT have one in the PRIOR year -- i.e. new/incident diagnoses, not the cumulative/prevalent diagnosed population -- confirmed with the user. This is why it is markedly smaller than epic_n_patients_hepc (crosstab 1, the cumulative diagnosed population as of that year: roughly 12-35% of it nationally, varying by year) and why it declines toward the present (167,148 nationally in 2018 down to 64,861 in 2025) even as epic_n_patients_hepc grows over the same span (471,746 to 561,496): fewer NEW diagnoses each year, while the prevalent pool keeps accumulating. Do not treat this as comparable to epic_n_patients_hepc or epic_n_patients_hepc_medication_pop -- it is a different (smaller, incident) population entirely. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed and imputed as 5, flagged by epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis_suppressed_flag. The most recent period (2026, partial year Jan 1 - Sep 1) is suppressed in EVERY one of the 5 geographies for this measure and all 5 percentage measures built on it -- confirmed directly in the raw export (every cell reads blank or "10 or fewer"), consistent with a partial year producing fewer new diagnoses than a full year, on top of the declining incidence trend.
epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis.statement: In {location}, {value} patients were newly diagnosed with hepatitis C in {time} (no prior-year diagnosis).

epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis_suppr.long_description: 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the cell (a count of 10 or fewer) and the value was imputed as 5; 0 otherwise. Computed before imputation. Where this flag is 1, all 5 percentage measures built on this population (see epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis) are deliberately left missing rather than asserting a meaningless 5 / 5 = 100%. Every geography is flagged 1 for the most recent partial period (2026) -- see the note under epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis.
epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis_suppr.statement: In {location}, the new-HCV-diagnosis count for {time} was suppressed and imputed ({value}).

Where the underlying count was suppressed, the imputed rate is 5 / epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis * 100, flagged by epic_pct_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis_suppressed_flag. The most recent period (2026 partial year) is suppressed in every geography -- see epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis's note. This is the first stage-1 branch of the care cascade built from this crosstab; epic_n_patients_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis is the corresponding DERIVED patient count, and is the denominator for epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_diagnosis.

epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_d.long_name: Percent of antiviral-treated, newly diagnosed hepatitis C patients with a normal HCV viral load result more than 20 weeks after treatment
epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_d.short_description: Rate of a normal HCV viral load result, 20+ weeks after antiviral treatment, among patients newly diagnosed that year who received antivirals after diagnosis.
epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_d.long_description: RECONDITIONED 2026-09-21, per explicit user direction: the source reports this rate (session 2857569's "Normal hep c test after meds, 20 weeks (%)" column) against the full new-diagnosis population, epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis -- despite its name implying a narrower, already-treated population. To build a true sequential care cascade, this ingest instead re-expresses it as (source-reported numerator count) / epic_n_patients_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis * 100, i.e. among patients who actually received antivirals after diagnosis, not among all newly diagnosed patients regardless of treatment status. The numerator count itself is only recoverable via the source's own rate against the full population (5 / epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis * 100 when suppressed and the population is not), so it is backed out that way first, then capped at epic_n_patients_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis (the two are independently rounded by the source and can rarely disagree by a patient or two) and re-divided by it. Still NOT the medication-restricted, prevalent population used for epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_hcv_medication (crosstab 4, session 2857341) -- that measure's population is the cumulative/prevalent diagnosed population, not a single year's new diagnoses; do not chart the two as a continuous series. Left NA when either the source rate or epic_n_patients_hepc_meds_after_diagnosis was itself suppressed (flagged by epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_diagnosis_suppressed_flag). The most recent period (2026 partial year) is suppressed in every geography -- see epic_n_patients_hepc_new_diagnosis's note; a 20-week-later outcome measure is especially sensitive to this since the window itself has often not yet elapsed for a partial year.
epic_pct_normal_vl_20wk_after_meds_new_d.statement: In {location}, {value}% of patients newly diagnosed with hepatitis C in {time} who received antivirals had a normal HCV VL result more than 20 weeks after treatment.

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'
